questions.question: IBM 370 was a _________ generation computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__ generation computer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• IBM 370 series, introduced in 1970, belongs to the 3rd generation of computers.
 
• 3rd generation computers used Integrated Circuits (ICs) to replace transistors, leading to more compact and efficient systems.
 
• These computers were characterized by the use of semiconductor memory and operating systems capable of multitasking and time-sharing.
 
• IBM 370 was known for being one of the first computers to support virtual memory, which allowed for more efficient processing and use of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation Computers (1940-1956)**

 
 
• These computers used vacuum tubes for circuitry and magnetic drums for memory.
 
• They were very large, consumed a lot of power, and produced a lot of heat.
 
• Examples include ENIAC, UNIVAC.
 
 
 
• **Second Generation Computers (1956-1963)**
 
 
• These computers used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, making them smaller, faster, and more reliable.
 
• They also used magnetic core memory.
 
• Examples include IBM 1401 and IBM 7090.
 
 
 
• **Third Generation Computers (1964-1971)**
 
 
• Integrated Circuits (ICs) were used in these computers, which significantly increased the speed and efficiency.
 
• They also introduced operating systems and multiprogramming.
 
• Examples include IBM 360 and IBM 370.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Generation Computers (1971-Present)**
 
 
• These computers use microprocessors, which contain thousands of integrated circuits on a single silicon chip.
 
• They are characterized by the development of personal computers (PCs).
 
• Examples include Apple II, IBM PC.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Generation Computers (Present and Beyond)**
 
 
• These computers are based on artificial intelligence and use parallel processing and superconductors.
 
• They aim to develop devices that respond to natural language input and are capable of learning and self-organization.
 
• Examples include AI systems, advanced robotics.

questions.question: ENIAC, the first electronics digital programmable computer device (1943), stands for ________.

options.text: Electronic Numerical Integrator and Analytical Computer

questions.solution:
Source Code:

The correct answer is __**Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ENIAC** stands for **Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer**.
 
• ENIAC was the first electronic digital programmable computer device developed in the year **1943**.
 
• It was designed and built by **John W. Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert** at the University of Pennsylvania.
 
• ENIAC was capable of performing complex calculations much faster than any prior human or mechanical computing methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of ENIAC**

 
 
• ENIAC, short for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, was a groundbreaking machine in the history of computing.
 
• It was developed during World War II and was primarily used for calculating artillery firing tables for the United States Army's Ballistic Research Laboratory.
 
• ENIAC's development began in 1943 and was completed in 1945. It was unveiled to the public in 1946.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications of ENIAC**
 
 
• ENIAC was composed of 17,468 vacuum tubes, 7,200 crystal diodes, 1,500 relays, 70,000 resistors, and 10,000 capacitors.
 
• The machine consumed about 150 kilowatts of electrical power and could perform around 5,000 additions per second.
 
• ENIAC was reprogrammable, which meant it could be reconfigured to solve different types of problems, albeit through manual rewiring and setting of switches.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Legacy of ENIAC**
 
 
• ENIAC demonstrated the feasibility and potential of electronic digital computing, paving the way for future advancements in computer science and technology.
 
• The concepts and technologies developed for ENIAC influenced subsequent computer designs and contributed to the evolution of modern computers.
 
• ENIAC's success also spurred interest and investment in further research and development of electronic computing systems.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures in ENIAC's Development**
 
 
• John W. Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert were the primary designers and engineers behind ENIAC.
 
• They collaborated with a team of engineers, including women mathematicians known as "computers," who played an essential role in programming and operating ENIAC.
 
• After the success of ENIAC, Mauchly and Eckert continued to make significant contributions to the field of computing, including the development of the UNIVAC I, one of the first commercially available computers.

questions.question: What does ASCII stand for?

options.text: American Standard Code for Internet Information
Asian Schema Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Internet Interchange

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII)** is a character encoding standard for electronic communication.
 
• ASCII codes represent text in computers, telecommunications equipment, and other devices that use text.
 
• Each letter, digit, or symbol is assigned a number from 0 to 127.
 
• For example, the ASCII code for uppercase **A** is **65**, and for lowercase **a** is **97**.
 
• It was developed from telegraph code and first published as a standard in 1963.
 
• ASCII is now largely replaced by Unicode, which includes ASCII as a subset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASCII** originally used 7 bits to represent each character, allowing for 128 unique symbols.
 
• Extended ASCII uses 8 bits, allowing for 256 symbols, which includes additional characters for graphical symbols and foreign language letters.
 
• ASCII has been incorporated into many other coding schemes, such as UTF-8, which is compatible with ASCII and can represent any character in the Unicode standard.
 
• The widespread adoption of ASCII has ensured that text files can be easily shared and understood across different types of computer systems.

questions.question: What was the first computer created by JW Mauchly and J Presper Eckert with NO mechanical parts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ENIAC**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first computer created by J.W. Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert with no mechanical parts was the ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer).
 
• **ENIAC** was developed in **1945** and was the **first general-purpose, fully electronic digital computer**.
 
• It used **vacuum tubes** for computation instead of mechanical components or relays, making it much faster than earlier mechanical or electromechanical computers.
 
• ENIAC was used primarily for military purposes, such as calculating artillery firing tables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mark II**:
 
• The **Mark II** was an **electromechanical computer** built after the Mark I.
 
• It used relays and mechanical parts, so it was slower and less advanced compared to ENIAC.
 
• Created under the guidance of **Howard Aiken** at Harvard University.
 
• **EDVAC (Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer)**:
 
• EDVAC was an advancement over ENIAC and was designed by Mauchly and Eckert as well.
 
• It introduced the concept of **stored programs**, as suggested by **John von Neumann**.
 
• It was completed in **1952**, after ENIAC.
 
• **Mark I (Harvard Mark I)**:
 
• The Harvard Mark I was an **electromechanical computer** built in **1944** by Howard Aiken with funding from IBM.
 
• It was a pioneering machine but relied heavily on mechanical relays, unlike ENIAC, which was fully electronic.

questions.question: 1 EB is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1024 PB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• EB stands for Exabyte, which is a unit of digital information storage.
 
• 1 Exabyte (EB) is equal to 1024 Petabytes (PB).
 
• Petabyte (PB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 1024 Terabytes (TB).
 
• Exabyte is often used to measure data storage capacity for large-scale data centers and cloud storage services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exabyte (EB)**

 
 
• An Exabyte (EB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^18 bytes (1,000,000,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Petabytes (PB).
 
• EB is used to describe large data sets and is often utilized in the context of big data, data warehouses, and cloud storage.
 
• For example, it is estimated that all the words ever spoken by humans would take up about 5 Exabytes of storage.
 
 
 
• **Petabyte (PB)**
 
 
• A Petabyte (PB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^15 bytes (1,000,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Terabytes (TB).
 
• PB is commonly used to measure the amount of data in large databases and data warehouses.
 
• For example, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) generates about 15 Petabytes of data annually.
 
 
 
• **Terabyte (TB)**
 
 
• A Terabyte (TB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10^12 bytes (1,000,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Gigabytes (GB).
 
• TB is commonly used to measure the storage capacity of hard drives and other storage devices.
 
• For example, a modern laptop may have a storage capacity of 1 to 2 Terabytes.
 
 
 
• **Gigabyte (GB)**
 
 
• A Gigabyte (GB) is a unit of digital information storage equal to 10⁹ bytes (1,000,000,000 bytes) or 1024 Megabytes (MB).
 
• GB is commonly used to measure the size of files, such as videos, photos, and software applications.
 
• For example, a high-definition movie may take up about 4 to 5 Gigabytes of storage.

questions.question: In Computer terminology, ALU stands for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arithmetic Logic Unit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** is a crucial component of the central processing unit (CPU) in a computer.
 
• The ALU is responsible for performing arithmetic and logical operations, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and logical comparisons.
 
• It is a fundamental building block of the CPU and plays a significant role in the execution of instructions.
 
• ALUs are designed to handle binary data and execute operations based on the instructions provided by the control unit of the CPU.
 
• The efficiency and speed of the ALU directly impact the overall performance of the computer system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ALU is a key component in both simple and complex processors, from microcontrollers to advanced microprocessors.
 
• Modern CPUs may contain multiple ALUs to enhance processing power and enable parallel execution of instructions.
 
• In addition to basic arithmetic and logic functions, advanced ALUs may support operations like bitwise shifts, rotations, and complex mathematical functions.
 
• The design and architecture of the ALU can vary depending on the specific requirements and applications of the processor.
 
• Understanding the functionality of the ALU is essential for computer engineers and anyone involved in computer architecture and design.

• OMR is accomplished using a hardware device (scanner) that detects a reflection or limited light transmittance on or through a piece of paper.
 
• OMR allows for the processing of hundreds or thousands of documents per hour.
 
• For example, students may recall taking tests or surveys where they filled in bubbles on paper (shown right) with a pencil.
 
• Once the form had been completed, a teacher or teacher's assistant would feed the cards into a system that grades or gathers information from them. 

***Hence the ******OMR is used in aptitude tests.***
